## Summary

This implements issue #197, adding Gmail Pub/Sub history synchronization as the Gmail-mode analogue of #196's bounded IMAP IDLE lifecycle:

- **`gmailWatchLifecycle.ts`** — `createGmailWatchLifecycleFactory` hosts two long-lived loops per account: a renewal loop that registers/renews `users.watch` daily (well inside its 7-day validity) and persists only `gmail_watch_expires_at` (never `gmail_history_id`, which stays `reconcileGmailAccount`'s exclusive write), and a pull loop that consumes Cloud Pub/Sub notifications, filters by the account's own email, and turns a match into the existing idempotent `enqueueMailAccountSync` call — acknowledging only after that durably commits.
- **`gmailPubSubClient.ts`** — the real fetch-based transport over Gmail's REST `users.watch` and Cloud Pub/Sub's REST pull/acknowledge endpoints, following the same "untested in CI, no live GCP project" precedent as `gmailRestClient.ts`.
- **`mailAccountSyncStateStore.ts`** — added `recordGmailWatchExpiry`, a single-purpose writer scoped to just the watch-expiry column.
- **`gmailWatchLifecycle.test.ts`** — 8 tests against a fake transport and the real test Postgres, covering registration/persistence, notification handling and jobKey dedup, account-validation filtering, duplicate/redelivery safety, pull-error backoff, renewal cadence, and stop() semantics.

Type-check is clean, and the new tests pass consistently across isolated and full-suite runs. The full suite otherwise passes except for intermittent `out of shared memory` Postgres errors in the embedded test cluster, which hit a different, non-overlapping set of unrelated pre-existing test files on each run and pass cleanly when re-run in isolation — confirmed as environment resource contention, not a regression from this change.

## Summary

This implements issue #197 (Gmail Pub/Sub history synchronization), the Gmail-mode analogue of #196's bounded IMAP IDLE lifecycle:

- **`gmailWatchLifecycle.ts`** — `createGmailWatchLifecycleFactory` hosts two long-lived loops per account: a renewal loop that registers/renews `users.watch` daily and persists both the expiry and (on first registration only) the history cursor, and a pull loop that consumes Cloud Pub/Sub notifications, validates them against the account's own email, and hands matches off to the existing idempotent `enqueueMailAccountSync` job — acknowledging only after that durably commits.
- **`gmailPubSubClient.ts`** — the real transport over Gmail's REST `users.watch` and Cloud Pub/Sub's REST pull/acknowledge endpoints, with a bounded response reader, explicit field validation instead of unchecked type casts, and per-notification error isolation so one malformed message can't block an entire pull batch.
- **`mailAccountSyncStateStore.ts`** — `recordGmailWatchRegistration` persists the watch expiry unconditionally and seeds the history cursor via `COALESCE` only when none exists yet, satisfying the "persist history/expiry" requirement without letting a later renewal regress a cursor the reconcile pass has since advanced.
- **`gmailWatchLifecycle.test.ts`** — 9 tests covering registration/persistence (including the cursor-seeding and non-regression cases), notification handling and jobKey dedup, account-validation filtering, duplicate/redelivery safety, pull-error backoff, renewal cadence, and stop() semantics.

This round of commits also addresses all 4 findings from the automated code review on PR #280: removed dead test code, capped the Pub/Sub/Gmail response body size, replaced unchecked type casts with explicit field validation, isolated malformed-notification parsing so it can't fail an entire pull batch, and fixed the previously unmet acceptance criterion around persisting the `users.watch` historyId.

Type-check is clean. The full backend suite passes except for intermittent `out of shared memory` Postgres errors in the embedded test cluster under full-suite concurrency, which hit a different, non-overlapping set of unrelated pre-existing files each run and pass cleanly (116/116) when re-run together with this issue's own tests in isolation — confirmed as environment resource contention, not a regression from this change.
This issue was resolved by #280, which just merged into develop.
